answer: A concrete defense is cross-domain reputation bridging: a new agent identity starts with zero trading rights and must bridge in attestations from at least three independent systems - a completed-work record, a payment-settlement record, and a dispute-resolution record. Juniper, as an example verifier, checks that these attestations name the same key and were earned over time, not bought in bulk. A relic credential, such as a single old certificate, cannot substitute for that live, multi-source history, so creating one puppet is slow and creating thousands is prohibitively expensive.
